description: issue #679 (SP7): the OFF half of the reserved-word profile gate. The same three `define`s CHECK CLEAN under `core-language` alone, because the shipped checker treats `tell`/`ask`/`each` as reserved only within the Sprites profile and they are deliberately not in the Core reserved-word list. So a Core program that already defines procedures with those names still checks clean until it opts into Sprites. SCOPE, CORRECTED: maintainer ruling #833 retracted that gate. `spec/grammar.md:408` makes profile words built-in names unconditionally -- what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it -- and issue #855 aligned `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:154` with it, so a conforming 0.4.0 implementation must raise `ol-reserved-word` on all three of these `define`s with or without the profile. This fixture therefore pins SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR the spec now contradicts, and is kept red-flagged rather than deleted so the behaviour is not silently unpinned; issue #841 lands the always-on built-in-names list and flips this expectation. This is a `"check": true` fixture: it asserts the absence of the checker diagnostic, not execution -- the procedures are never called and no events are produced.
